climate.overview_html: The diplomatic centre of gravity shifts to New York on September 22–23: UNGA 81’s High-Level General Debate opened today with 193 heads of state and government addressing the green-marble podium; US President Trump and French President Macron are among today’s early speakers, with climate, energy costs, and the Nepal catastrophe expected to feature prominently. Secretary-General Guterres convenes the Climate Summit 2026 tomorrow, September 23, focused on accelerating the just energy transition, mobilising climate finance for developing nations, and protecting people from an accelerating crisis — ten years after Paris, the first summit framing climate overshoot as already locked in rather than to be avoided. The scientific backdrop has grown more urgent: updated multi-model ensembles now give a 75% probability that the 2026 event will be the strongest El Niño on record (since 1950), with an OND 2026 median forecast of +2.67°C and a 98% probability of the Super El Niño phase persisting October–December. In Nepal, the Nepali government’s focus has officially shifted to “rehabilitation” as confirmed deaths reach approximately 1,280 by official government count (with ~3,916 still missing) and at least 48 suspension bridges destroyed. Europe’s EFFIS total reached 669,118 ha as of this week’s update, slightly above the 668,035 ha figure on September 16–17 and nearly double the 20-year average.

items.source: United Nations / UN News / CNN / PBS NewsHour
items.headline: UNGA 81 General Debate Opens September 22: 193 Leaders at the Podium; Trump and Macron Among First-Day Speakers; Climate, Nepal, Energy Costs Central — Guterres Climate Summit 2026 Tomorrow September 23: Energy Transition, Climate Finance, Overshoot
items.summary: UNGA 81's High-Level General Debate opened September 22, 2026, with 193 member state heads of state and government addressing the Assembly through September 28. US President Trump and French President Macron are among the first-day speakers; climate, soaring energy prices, and the Nepal-Tibet glacier catastrophe are expected to dominate their interventions. The General Debate runs under the session theme 'Restoring trust, managing transformation: A United Nations that delivers for all.' Secretary-General Guterres will convene the Climate Summit 2026 on Wednesday September 23 — an interactive leaders' dialogue plus thematic solutions dialogues focused on three pillars: (1) accelerating the just and orderly energy transition; (2) mobilising affordable climate finance and investments for developing countries (investment needs: USD 3.1–3.5 trillion per year by 2030); and (3) delivering adaptation and resilience in an era of climate overshoot. This is the first UN climate summit to explicitly frame 1.5°C overshoot as already locked in — a significant diplomatic and scientific threshold. Climate Week NYC continues in parallel through September 27 with more than 1,000 events.

items.headline: WMO Global Seasonal Climate Update SON 2026: Niño 3.4 ~+3.6°C; Positive IOD +0.9°C; Above-Normal Temperatures Forecast Most Land Areas September–November; Super El Niño at Peak Season
items.summary: WMO's Global Seasonal Climate Update for September–November 2026 places the Niño 3.4 index at approximately +3.6°C above average, consistent with the confirmed Super El Niño at or approaching its seasonal peak. The co-occurring positive Indian Ocean Dipole at +0.9°C amplifies drought risk over Indonesia, the Philippines, and eastern Australia while increasing rainfall risk over eastern Africa and the Horn. Above-normal temperatures are forecast for most global land areas in SON 2026, with significant probability of record-breaking warmth in the tropics and sub-tropics. WMO confirms 2027 remains the likely warmest calendar year on record as the El Niño peak contribution propagates into NH winter 2026/27.

items.headline: Super El Niño Forecast UPDATED: 75% Probability of Strongest on Record (Since 1950); OND 2026 Median Peak +2.67°C; 98% Probability of Super El Niño Phase Through October–December; Spring 2027 Neutral Transition 55% Chance
items.summary: Updated NOAA CPC and IRI multi-model ensemble forecasts published in the September 2026 ENSO update give a 75% probability that the current Super El Niño will surpass the 1997–98 event (+2.6°C peak) to become the strongest on record since 1950. The median OND 2026 forecast is +2.67°C for the Niño 3.4 index. There is a 98% probability of the Super El Niño phase persisting through October–December 2026. Climate scientist Daniel Swain (UCLA/WeatherWest) placed the probability at ~70% of this being the strongest event on record. A 55% probability of returning to neutral phase by April–June 2027 suggests a sharp El Niño-to-neutral or El Niño-to-La Niña transition, consistent with historical post-Super El Niño patterns. Continued Atlantic hurricane season suppression, drought deepening in eastern Australia, Indonesia, and SE Asia, and enhanced rainfall over the Horn of Africa and the US Gulf Coast remain the near-term impact projections.

items.source: Nepal NDRRMA / Wikipedia / Al Jazeera / ABC News
items.headline: Nepal–Tibet Glacier Collapse Floods UPDATED September 22: Government Shifts to “Rehabilitation” Phase; Official Confirmed Dead ~1,280; Missing ~3,916; 48 Suspension Bridges Destroyed; ~75 US Nationals Still Unaccounted For; $820M+ International Pledges
items.summary: Nepal's Nepali prime minister announced September 22 that the government's focus would shift to 'rehabilitation' — a signal that the acute rescue phase is winding down. Official Nepali government confirmed dead stands at approximately 1,280; approximately 3,916 are still classified as missing. The US State Department confirmed it is tracking approximately 75 American nationals unaccounted for in the Nepal-Tibet cross-border region. At least 48 suspension bridges were destroyed, severely hampering access to remote mountain communities. International pledges reached $820 million. Nepal's parliament's national climate emergency declaration remains active. A formal UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund submission — the first to directly implicate European-origin emissions in a Himalayan glacier catastrophe — is active as world leaders gather at UNGA. ICIMOD found the Yanmarang Glacier lost approximately 40% of its volume since 2020.

items.source: Geophysical Research Letters / AGU / PIK Potsdam
items.headline: “Global Warming Has Accelerated Significantly” — Foster & Rahmstorf GRL Vol. 53 Issue 17; First Statistically Confirmed Acceleration Since ~2015 at >98% Confidence; Faster Than Any Prior Decade in 177-Year Record After ENSO/Volcanic/Solar Removal Across Five Temperature Datasets
items.summary: Foster and Rahmstorf apply natural-variability filtering across five global temperature datasets (NASA GISTEMP, NOAA GlobalTemp, HadCRUT5, Berkeley Earth, ERA5) to isolate the forced warming signal from ENSO, volcanic, and solar variability. The residual shows, for the first time with greater than 98% statistical confidence, that global warming has accelerated since approximately 2015 at a rate faster than any previous decade in the 177-year record. The implied non-linearity is consistent with compound forcing from cumulative CO₂, declining reflective aerosol loading as Asian coal combustion falls, and positive ice-albedo and water vapor feedbacks. The result directly strengthens the attribution basis for climate damage claims, including the Nepal–Tibet UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund submission active at UNGA — framing it as the capstone scientific finding of Climate Week NYC 2026.

items.headline: Europe Just Had Its Hottest Summer on Record — Western Europe 2.54°C Above 1991–2020 Normal; Rhine at 1880 Historic Low; 2,025+ Excess Deaths France; Farm Income Down ~9%; Paks and Cernavodă Nuclear Curtailed
items.summary: Analysis quantifies the cascading economic and humanitarian damage of Europe's record summer 2026 — the hottest in recorded history for western Europe at 2.54°C above the 1991–2020 Copernicus climatology. France recorded its hottest summer ever with 2,025+ excess deaths. The Rhine fell to its lowest navigational level since 1880, pushing freight costs 18–25% above seasonal norms. Low Danube water forced Hungary's Paks nuclear plant and Romania's Cernavodă plant to curtailed output. French farm income declined approximately 9% from crop failures.

weather.overview_html: Typhoon Dujuan’s extratropical transition is now underway: the system has moved to 37.8°N 146.0°E off Tohoku’s Pacific coast and transition is forecast to complete by 09:00 JST September 23. Oshima Island recorded 600 mm of rainfall in the 24 hours ending 14:00 LT September 21 — a record for any storm event at the site; flooding, landslides, and transport disruption continued across Kanto into September 22. In the Atlantic: Tropical Storm Fay remains active approximately 405 miles southwest of the Azores with maximum sustained winds of 65 mph as of September 22; NHC forecasts a brief possible intensification before the system becomes a post-tropical remnant low September 23–24; no land threat is posed. With no hurricane yet by September 22, the 2026 Atlantic season has now set the longest no-hurricane run in the satellite era, overtaking the previous record of September 18, 1966 — entirely attributable to Super El Niño-driven vertical wind shear suppression. All other events (SE Asia haze, European wildfires, Nepal floods, Pakistan monsoon) show no material new development as of September 22 morning.

items.headline: Typhoon No. 25 Dujuan UPDATED September 22: Extratropical Transition Underway at 37.8°N 146.0°E; Oshima Records 600 mm/24 h (Record); Flooding & Landslides Kanto; ET Completion Forecast 09:00 JST September 23
items.summary: Typhoon Dujuan has moved to 37.8°N, 146.0°E off the Tohoku Pacific coast as of September 22, where it sits on the equatorward edge of the upper-level jet and has begun extratropical transition. JMA forecasts transition to complete by 09:00 JST September 23, when the center will be near 42.6°N, 161.6°E — well east of Hokkaido. Oshima Island recorded 600 mm of rainfall in the 24 hours ending 14:00 LT September 21, a station record for any storm event. Flooding, landslides, and transport disruption across the Kanto region continued into September 22. The extratropical low is then forecast to track northeast and dissipate over the Northwest Pacific. Dujuan made landfall on the Boso Peninsula (Chiba Prefecture) on September 21 with 126 km/h sustained winds and 180 km/h gusts — the strongest Kanto landfall since 2019.

items.source: Washington Post / NHC / WFTV / Fox Weather
items.headline: Tropical Storm Fay UPDATED September 22: Active ~405 mi SW Azores; 65 mph Sustained; Possible Brief Intensification; Post-Tropical September 23–24; No Land Threat; 2026 Atlantic Now Record Longest Without a Hurricane (Beats September 18, 1966)
items.summary: Tropical Storm Fay remains active as of September 22, centered approximately 405 miles southwest of the Azores, moving south-southeast at 2 mph with maximum sustained winds of 65 mph. NHC notes possible brief intensification before gradual weakening; the system is forecast to become a post-tropical remnant low September 23–24 with no land threats or coastal hazards. With no Atlantic hurricane having formed through September 22, the 2026 season has set the record for the longest no-hurricane run in the satellite era, surpassing September 18, 1966. The absence of hurricanes is attributable to Super El Niño-driven vertical wind shear across the main development region — consistent with pre-season outlooks that forecast below-normal activity.

items.source: Time / ASMC ASEAN / Mongabay / ABC News Australia
items.headline: SE Asia Wildfire Haze ONGOING: 12 Million People Blanketed; 113,336 Respiratory Cases Indonesia (Sept 9); Japan CH-47 Chinooks Kalimantan Sept 12–19; Worst Indonesian Wildfires in 11 Years; Fires Through October/November
items.summary: No material update September 18–22. Status as of September 17: more than 12 million people blanketed in thick smog across Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam. Indonesia's Health Ministry recorded 113,336 respiratory infection cases across seven provinces as of September 9. At least 200,000+ hectares burned across Borneo and Sumatra. Japan CH-47 Chinooks remained deployed in West Kalimantan through September 19. On September 14 Kuala Lumpur, Singapore, and Kuching ranked 1–3 globally for worst air quality. ASEAN Level 3 (highest) alert remains active. Indonesian authorities warn fires could continue through October or early November under Super El Niño-driven late rainy season suppression.

items.headline: Europe Wildfires UPDATED: EFFIS Total Now 669,118 ha (Week of September 22); Slightly Above 668,035 ha on September 16–17; Nearly Double 20-Year Average of 346,567 ha; Worst Season Since 2017
items.summary: EFFIS (European Forest Fire Information System) data updated in the week of September 22 places the 2026 European burned area total at 669,118 hectares — a marginal increase from the 668,035 ha figure cited on September 16–17. The total remains nearly double the 20-year average (2006–2025) of 346,567 hectares and represents the worst wildfire season since 2017. The season is driven by western Europe's hottest summer on record (2.54°C above the 1991–2020 average) and drought accumulating since early spring. Extreme fire danger continues in the Iberian Peninsula, Pyrenees, and western Balkans.

items.headline: Pakistan NDMA Flood Alert ONGOING: Monsoon Death Toll 234+ Dead / 596+ Injured; GB, KPK, Punjab, Balochistan Flash Flood Risk; Final Monsoon Active Phase Through Late September
items.summary: No new NDMA update found September 18–22. Status as of September 15: nationwide monsoon death toll 234 dead and 596 injured since late June. Flash flood risks cover Gilgit-Baltistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab, and Balochistan. Urban flooding continues in Lahore, Faisalabad, and Rawalpindi. Final monsoon active phase extends through late September. Children accounted for 82 of the 180 deaths recorded by September 3 per NDMA data.

renewables.overview_html: The week adds a major construction milestone for European offshore wind: all four offshore substation topsides and support frames for the 1.5 GW Baltica 2 wind farm (Ørsted + PGE) departed PTSC M&C’s Ho Chi Minh City yard on September 12–14 and are now in transit to the Polish Baltic — where Seaway7 will install them from November 2026, unlocking turbine installation for Poland’s first large-scale offshore wind project (107×14 MW Siemens Gamesa; commissioning 2027). The prior week’s flagship grid infrastructure contract remains 50Hertz awarding NSORe + Siemens Energy the LanWin3 2 GW North Sea HVDC offshore converter platform on September 18 — NSORe’s second 2 GW 50Hertz contract in 2026, combined LanWin3 + LanWin6 value approximately €2.5 billion. South Korea’s offshore supply chain continued its acceleration: LS Marine Solution’s 156.9 billion won (~US$114 million) submarine cable contract for the 390 MW Sinan Wooi farm (September 18) — its largest-ever order and the first project in South Korea’s 8.2 GW Sinan belt. Africa’s largest renewable contract for the year: EnerSynk + ZESCO’s 25-year, 500 MW Zambia Copperbelt PPA (September 16).

items.headline: Four Baltica 2 Offshore Substations Set Sail from Vietnam to Poland — All 4 Topsides + Support Frames Depart PTSC M&C Ho Chi Minh City September 12–14; Seaway7 Installation November 2026; 1.5 GW Ørsted + PGE; 107×14 MW Siemens Gamesa; Commissioning 2027
items.summary: All four offshore substation topsides and matching support frames for the 1.5 GW Baltica 2 offshore wind farm departed PTSC Mechanical & Construction's shipyard near Ho Chi Minh City between September 12–14, 2026, and are now in transit to the Polish Baltic Sea. Each substation weighs approximately 3,500 tonnes and spans five floors, with a rated capacity of 375 MW each. Seaway7 will install all four substations under a transportation and installation contract beginning November 2026. The Baltica 2 project comprises 107 Siemens Gamesa 14-222 wind turbines (14 MW each) and is developed jointly by Ørsted and PGE — Poland's largest offshore wind project and the first to receive backing from South Korea's-style national investment vehicle. Full commissioning is planned for end 2027. Vietnam's PTSC M&C has cemented its role in the European offshore wind supply chain with this delivery, following earlier work on North Sea and UK projects.

items.headline: 50Hertz Awards LanWin3 2 GW North Sea HVDC Converter Platform Contract to NSORe + Siemens Energy — Second 2 GW NSORe/50Hertz Contract in 2026; Combined LanWin3 + LanWin6 Value ~€2.5 Billion to NSORe; Topside Rostock-Warnemünde, Jacket Vlissingen
items.summary: German transmission system operator 50Hertz awarded the LanWin3 North Sea offshore HVDC converter platform contract to the Neptun Werft–Smulders Offshore Renewables (NSORe) joint venture and Siemens Energy on September 18. This is NSORe's second major 50Hertz contract in 2026, following the LanWin6 award in June. Siemens Energy supplies the high-voltage components; NSORe handles system design, procurement, construction, offshore installation, and commissioning. The topside is fabricated at Neptun Werft in Rostock-Warnemünde, Germany; the steel jacket at Smulders in Vlissingen, the Netherlands. Combined contract value attributable to NSORe for LanWin3 and LanWin6 totals approximately €2.5 billion.

items.headline: LS Marine Solution Wins 156.9 Billion Won (~US$114 M) Submarine Cable Contract for 390 MW Sinan Wooi Offshore Wind Farm — South Korea’s First National Growth Fund Offshore Wind Project; Largest-Ever LS Marine Order (2.2× FY2025 Revenue); First Project in 8.2 GW Sinan Offshore Wind Belt; Cable Installation 2026–2028
items.summary: LS Marine Solution secured a 156.9 billion Korean won (approximately US$114 million) contract on September 18 to supply and install submarine power cables for the 390 MW Sinan Wooi offshore wind farm — its largest-ever order at 2.2 times its full-year FY2025 revenue. Sinan Wooi is the first project to receive funding from South Korea's National Growth Fund specifically for offshore wind, and marks the opening project in the government-designated 8.2 GW Sinan offshore wind development belt. Cable installation is scheduled 2026–2028.

items.headline: Zambia Inks 25-Year PPA for 500 MW Solar Project — EnerSynk + ZESCO Copperbelt; Zambia’s Largest-Ever Renewable Contract; Replaces Drought-Hit Zambezi Hydropower for Copper Industry
items.summary: EnerSynk and ZESCO Ltd signed a 25-year PPA on September 16 for a 500 MW solar PV project in Zambia's Copperbelt — the country's largest-ever renewable energy contract. The project specifically targets the copper-mining industry's power supply chain, which accounts for approximately 70% of Zambia's total power demand. The plant reduces ZESCO's dependence on hydropower repeatedly curtailed in 2026 by drought driven by the positive IOD and Super El Niño.

items.headline: UK Secretary of State Approves DCO for Morecambe (480 MW) + Morgan Offshore Wind Transmission Assets — Full Consent Package Complete; Export Cables, Substations + Grid to Penwortham; >500,000 UK Households
items.summary: UK Secretary of State approved the Development Consent Order for transmission assets serving both the 480 MW Morecambe and co-located Morgan offshore wind farms on September 15. The consent covers offshore export cables, landfall infrastructure, onshore cables, substations, and grid connection to the National Grid substation at Penwortham, Lancashire, completing the full regulatory package for Morecambe. The 35-turbine project will power over 500,000 UK households.

items.source: Renewable Energy Magazine / reNEWS / Yahoo Finance
items.headline: Econergy Acquires Escofi — 740 MW French Onshore Wind Platform for €134.3 Million: 128 MW Operational, 34 MW Under Construction, 578 MW in Development; >90% Operating Capacity Under 20-Year French CfDs at >€80/MWh; Econergy’s Entry into France
items.summary: Econergy Ltd acquired Escofi, a private French onshore wind developer founded in 1988, for €134.3 million on September 15 — Econergy's entry into France. Escofi's 740 MW portfolio: 128 MW operational, 34 MW under construction (target 2027), 147 MW advanced development, and 432 MW early-to-mid development. More than 90% of operational and under-construction capacity benefits from 20-year French CfDs at above €80/MWh.

science.overview_html: The September 15–16 publication cluster remains the window’s headline science output. Moore, Haqiqi, Kong et al. Nature Climate Change (September 16): heat-related labor productivity loss quantified at US$41/tonne CO2 (90% CI $1–108) — the second-largest SC-CO2 component after heat mortality, with agricultural damage revised down to $29/tonne CO2. Foster & Rahmstorf GRL Vol. 53 Issue 17 (September 16): >98%-confidence acceleration since ~2015, the fastest of any decade in the 177-year record across five datasets — now the scientific anchor of the Nepal UNFCCC Loss and Damage submission active at UNGA. Stratospheric chemistry: van Herpen et al. Nature Communications (September 15): Hunga Tonga Cl-radical CH4 oxidation at 900±220 Mg/day — a pathway absent from all CMIP7 models with implications for large-eruption and SAI scenarios. Two significant arXiv contributions from earlier in the window (ECMWF AIFS-CRPS+IMERG precipitation fine-tuning at arXiv:2609.03210; TailWeather global extremes benchmark at arXiv:2609.12496) have aged past the 7-day display window but remain archived. Noting also that the review “Bridging the weather and climate divide with artificial intelligence” (Nature Communications, August 18, 2026) — arguing AI is dissolving the forecasting/climate-modelling divide within a single unified Earth-system framework — is the most-cited new synthesis in the field this quarter even though it pre-dates the current 7-day window.

items.source: Nature Climate Change / UC Davis / phys.org
items.headline: Nature Climate Change: Heat-Related Labor Productivity Loss = US$41/tonne CO<sub>2</sub> (90% CI $1–108) in 2025 — Moore, Haqiqi, Kong et al.; Second-Largest SC-CO<sub>2</sub> Component After Heat Mortality; Agricultural Damage Revised Down to $29/tonne CO<sub>2</sub> Using AR6; Losses Concentrated South/East/SE Asia and Africa
items.meta: Moore, Haqiqi, Kong et al. · Nature Climate Change (2026) · doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02749-z · Published 16 September 2026
items.summary: Moore, Haqiqi, Kong et al. quantify heat-related labor productivity loss as a standalone component of the social cost of carbon, finding a central estimate of US$41 per tonne CO₂ (90% CI $1–108) when evaluated in 2025 dollars against a 2°C pathway. This makes labor productivity the second-largest SC-CO₂ component after heat mortality — a significant upward revision from prior estimates. Agricultural damage was simultaneously revised down from US$95 to US$29 per tonne CO₂ using IPCC AR6 methods and updated dose-response functions. Losses are geographically concentrated in South Asia, East Asia, Southeast Asia, and Sub-Saharan Africa — regions with both high outdoor labor shares and high climate vulnerability. The result has immediate implications for climate damage assessments used in litigation and regulatory cost-benefit analysis, including attribution arguments being advanced at UNGA this week.

items.source: Geophysical Research Letters / AGU / PIK Potsdam

The residual shows, for the first time with greater than 98% statistical confidence, that global warming has accelerated since approximately 2015 at a rate faster than any previous decade in the 177-year record. The implied non-linearity is consistent with compound forcing from cumulative CO₂, declining reflective aerosol loading as Asian coal combustion falls, and positive ice-albedo and water vapor feedbacks. The result directly strengthens the attribution basis for climate damage claims, including the Nepal–Tibet UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund submission active in this window.

items.headline: Nature Communications: Hunga Tonga Stratospheric Aerosol Layer Catalysed Anomalous CH<sub>4</sub> Oxidation at 900±220 Mg/day Via Cl-Radical Pathway — 12 ppb HCHO at 30 km; Pathway Absent From CMIP7 Models; Potential Net Cooling Offset in Large-Eruption/SAI Scenarios
items.meta: van Herpen et al. · Nature Communications (2026) · doi:10.1038/s41467-026-72191-4 · Published 15 September 2026
items.summary: Van Herpen et al. show that the 2022 Hunga Tonga eruption's stratospheric sulphate aerosol layer catalysed a previously uncharacterised methane-oxidation pathway involving Cl radicals produced at aerosol surfaces. Using ACE-FTS and MIPAS limb-emission satellite observations, the authors quantify CH₄ oxidation at 900 ± 220 Mg/day between 25–35 km altitude, sufficient to explain the anomalous HCHO column of ~12 ppb at 30 km (~8× background). The mechanism is absent from current CMIP7 chemistry–climate models; if triggered by large eruptions or proposed stratospheric aerosol injection, it could constitute a net cooling offset not captured in climate sensitivity assessments or geoengineering scenario modelling.

items.title: Rainmaker Raises $100 Million Series B for Drone-Based Cloud Seeding — Led by NOA VC + Upfront; DCVC, Lowercarbon, Dream Ventures Co-Invest; Pitches Cloud Seeding as Adaptation Tech for Data Center Water Demands and Drought Relief
items.body_html: Rainmaker, the El Segundo, California weather-modification startup, announced a $100 million Series B on September 21, 2026, led by NOA VC and Upfront Ventures with co-investment from DCVC, Lowercarbon Capital, and Dream Ventures — bringing total funding to $150.3 million since its 2023 founding. Rainmaker deploys a fleet of custom drones to seed clouds with silver iodide or other nucleating agents, with an atmospheric science and radar-specialist team determining optimal cloud targets, seeding timing, material volumes, and target precipitation zones; the company frames cloud seeding as climate adaptation rather than geoengineering, targeting drought relief in the American West, freshwater production for water-stressed municipalities, and — notably — cooling and humidification services for water-hungry hyperscale data centers. The data-centre angle — using cloud seeding to augment water availability near hyperscale campuses — is described by Hoodline as Rainmaker’s most commercially viable near-term pitch, exploiting the same data-center power and water demand that drove 34% of H1 2026 climate-tech VC to the Built Environment category. The round will fund expansion of Rainmaker’s atmospheric research team, drone fleet development, and commercial trials in the Southwest.
items.source_html: Fast Company / PR Newswire

items.title: CTVC / Currence H1’26 Climate Tech Report: $26.1 Billion Global VC Investment in H1 2026 (+55% YoY) — Data Centers Drive 34% of Total (vs. 3% in H1’25); Deal Count Hit 5-Year Low (-25%); Series A up 55% to $4.5 Bn on Nuclear Appetite; Adaptation Funding +64%
items.body_html: CTVC (now Currence), the climate-tech VC intelligence firm, published its H1’26 Climate Tech Investment & Innovation Report on September 21, 2026, finding total global venture investment in climate tech reached $26.1 billion in the first half of 2026 — up 55% year-on-year and the strongest first half since 2022 — driven overwhelmingly by data centre-related infrastructure. The Built Environment category grew more than 800% and overtook Energy as the largest funding vertical, with two Series C rounds (DayOne data centres: $4.5 billion; Nscale data centre operations: $2 billion) together accounting for nearly two-thirds of all Series C activity. Semafor framed the pattern as the “speed-to-power race”: as gas turbine lead times stretch to 5–8 years, data-center developers are driving demand for low-carbon firm power sources — advanced nuclear, superhot geothermal, long-duration storage — that can be contracted faster. Deal count simultaneously fell 25% to a 5-year low, with the 10 largest rounds taking 42% of all H1 2026 investment — reflecting capital concentration into proven-technology platforms. Series A was up 55% to $4.5 billion on appetite for nuclear (fission and fusion); adaptation funding rose 64% — the fastest-growing sub-vertical — consistent with the accelerating Super El Niño and record-insured-loss environment.

items.title: Cat Bond and ILS Market Bulletin (Week Ending September 20): MembersCap Launches First Cat Bond Fund + Novel ILW; Gallagher Securities Developing First-Ever New-Peril Cat Bond; CalPERS ILS Holdings Approach US$2.5 Billion — Fifth Consecutive Year of >$100 Billion Global Insured Nat-Cat Losses
items.body_html: The Artemis weekly bulletin for the week ending September 20, 2026 highlights three developments in the catastrophe bond and insurance-linked securities market: MembersCap has launched the first dedicated cat bond fund strategy alongside a novel industry loss warranty (ILW) structure designed to expand ILS investor access; Gallagher Securities is developing the first-ever cat bond covering a new, previously unbondable peril (specific peril undisclosed at launch), representing a structural expansion of the cat bond market’s risk frontier; and CalPERS’ insurance-linked securities holdings are approaching US$2.5 billion at mid-year 2026, cementing its position as the largest institutional investor in the cat bond asset class. The bulletin contextualises these developments against the fifth consecutive year of global insured natural catastrophe losses exceeding US$100 billion.

items.title: Mazama Energy Raises $135 Million Series B for Superhot Engineered Geothermal — Led by Centaurus Capital + Doerr Capital; ConocoPhillips, Shell Ventures, Khosla, Gates Frontier Co-Invest; Newberry Volcano, Oregon; Project Athena Drilling 750°F (400°C) Target
items.body_html: Mazama Energy, the Newberry Volcano (Oregon) superhot engineered geothermal system developer, raised $135 million in an oversubscribed Series B announced September 17, co-led by Centaurus Capital (John Arnold’s fund) and Doerr Capital. ConocoPhillips, Shell Ventures, Khosla Ventures, Gates Frontier, SiteGround Capital, H. Barton Asset Management, and the Jeffrey and Marieke Rothschild Foundation also participated. Mazama holds the record for the hottest engineered geothermal system ever built: a 629°F (331°C) EGS at Newberry in 2025; its second well, Project Athena, is drilling toward a 750°F (400°C) target where a single well can deliver up to 10× the power of a conventional 390°F well while using 75% less water and 80% fewer wells. The raise reflects growing major-oil-company conviction that superhot geothermal — with its baseload output profile and minimal surface footprint — can anchor firm-power supply in a grid increasingly dominated by variable renewables.

items.title: EU Climate Insurance Alliance — Von der Leyen State of the Union September 16: Only 25% of European Catastrophe Losses Currently Insured; Parametric + Group Instruments Proposed; 100 Vulnerable EU Regions to Be Mapped by October; Alliance Faces Criticism for Lacking Mandatory Cover Mandate
items.body_html: European Commission President von der Leyen announced the European Climate Insurance Alliance in her September 16 State of the Union address, citing data showing only 25% of European catastrophic climate losses are currently insured. The Alliance will develop group insurance pools for currently uninsurable catastrophe risks and expand parametric instruments — paying on measurable thresholds such as rainfall levels or temperatures — for agriculture, coastal flooding, and wildfire; the European Commission will map the 100 most-vulnerable EU regions by October 2026. The announcement follows Europe’s wildfire season reaching 669,118 ha per EFFIS, with uninsured losses estimated at €40–60 billion. Critics said the Alliance would not close the protection gap without mandatory natural-hazard cover.
items.source_html: Green Central Banking / The Insurer

items.title: Laki Power Raises €6 Million Series A Led by NATO Innovation Fund — Iceland Grid Monitoring Device Self-Powered From Live HV Lines; NIF’s First Iceland Investment; + ReykVC
items.body_html: Laki Power, a Reykjavík-based grid monitoring hardware company, closed a €6 million Series A on September 16 led by the NATO Innovation Fund with co-investment from ReykVC — NIF’s first investment in an Icelandic company. Laki Power’s core product is a grid monitoring device that harvests its operating power directly from live high-voltage transmission lines via inductive energy harvesting, eliminating external power supplies, batteries, or fibre-optic ground wires. The device provides real-time line-current, temperature, sag, and fault-location data; the self-powered design makes it viable for remote high-voltage corridors where conventional monitoring costs are prohibitive — directly relevant to Nordic and Arctic grid resilience and NATO dual-use energy security.
